title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
abstract: arXiv:2610.30798v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton. Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline. We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness. We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline. A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel. Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions. Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic. To identify exploitable bit-flip loc

translated_title: 通过Rowhammer攻击放大LLM推理的延迟与成本
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）通过诸如Triton等即时（JIT）编译框架生成的优化GPU内核来实现高推理效率。Triton通过基于MLIR/LLVM的流水线编译GPU内核。我们研究了CPU DRAM中由Rowhammer引起的位翻转是否能够在保持输出正确性的同时降低基于GPU的LLM推理性能。我们提出了LLVMhammer，这是首个通过在Triton编译流水线中诱导位翻转来导致LLM推理变慢的Rowhammer攻击。在性能关键优化过程中的一次位翻转会使Triton生成功能完全相同但次优的GPU内核。由于Triton将生成的内核缓存在磁盘上，一次成功的位翻转会导致后续推理执行的持续性能下降。Triton与目标无关的编译阶段在各GPU厂商之间共享，这使得我们的攻击不受GPU厂商限制。为了识别可利用的位翻转位置……（原文截断）
tldr: 本文提出LLVMhammer——首个针对Triton编译流水线的Rowhammer攻击，通过诱导性能关键优化阶段的位翻转，生成功能不变但性能次优的GPU内核，并借助内核磁盘缓存机制造成LLM推理的持久性变慢，且该攻击与GPU厂商无关。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that slows down LLM inference by inducing bit-flips in Triton's JIT compilation pipeline, producing functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernels whose on-disk caching enables persistent latency amplification independent of GPU vendor.
